title: POS category Vuex flow confirmed: posCategory/lists → GET /api/admin/pos-category → PosCategoryController@index
evidence: posCategory.js:33 `let url = 'admin/pos-category'`; routes/api.php:993-994 `Route::prefix('pos-category')->name('pos-category.')->group(function () { Route::get('/', [PosCategoryController::class, 'index']); });`; controller index() returns `['data' => $newObj]` where $newObj is array_merge(['all-items' sentinel], $itemCategories) with fields id/name/slug/description/status/thumb/cover (lines 114-131).
recommendation: Anchor verified — plan §1.1 file:line correct. Implementer can extend the response shape (add `featured` bool per item) at PosCategoryController.php:122-130 without breaking existing consumers (additive field).

title: item_categories schema: NO `is_featured` / `is_visible_on_pos` column exists — but `channels` JSON + `pos_sort` already gate POS surface filtering
evidence: DESCRIBE output columns: id, parent_id, name, kiosk_label, slug, description, status (default 5), channels (json nullable), sort, kiosk_sort, pos_sort (uint nullable), wizard_template, wizard_profile_id, has_menu, default_menu_kiosk, sauce_included_menu, kiosk_upsell_include, kiosk_upsell_skip_after_cart, deleted_at. NO featured/is_visible_on_pos column. Controller already filters: `whereNull('channels').orWhereJsonContains('channels','pos')` (lines 71-78). Sample data: only id=350 has channels=['pos','admin','mobile']; rest are NULL (so all default-show).
recommendation: No DDL needed. The cleanest source-of-truth IS a config-driven allowlist (plan §1.1 already chose this). `pos_sort` is currently NULL for all 13 sampled categories — using it as an allowlist signal would require seeding all 21 categories first, more invasive than `config/pos.php`.

title: items.is_featured is `Ask::YES` (=5), a Yes/No flag — brief's `defaults to 5 - misnamed Status` mischaracterization corrected
evidence: Ask.php:7 `const YES = 5;`. items migration line 31 `$table->tinyInteger('is_featured')->default(Ask::YES);`. DESCRIBE items: `is_featured tinyint NO 5`. The other column is items.status (default 5 = Status::ACTIVE). 2026_03_25_002927_add_is_upsell_to_items_table.php:10 docstring: 'Separate from is_featured (homepage) and is_popular (trending).'
recommendation: Plan's directive `DO NOT propose repurposing items.is_featured` still STANDS — but for the correct reason: it's an item-level homepage Yes/No flag, not a category-level mechanism. G1 needs a CATEGORY allowlist, so `is_featured` is the wrong layer regardless of its semantics. Confirm config-driven approach in §1.1.

title: Insertion point recommendation: BACKEND (PosCategoryController response shape) — single source of truth, no client knowledge duplication
evidence: Controller currently shapes the array per-category: `$itemCategoryArray[] = ['id' => $itemCategory->id, 'name' => ..., 'thumb' => ..., 'cover' => ...];` (lines 122-130). Adding a `'featured' => in_array((int)$itemCategory->id, (array) config('pos.featured_category_ids', []), true)` field is ~1 LOC + a stable `usort` on `[featured DESC, sort ASC]` before array_merge with the 'all-items' sentinel is ~3 LOC. PosComponent.vue:1415-1419 `categories` getter just reads `$store.getters['posCategory/lists']` — frontend stays dumb, only renders `featured===true` ones by default + a 'Toutes' toggle.
recommendation: Backend filter. Rationale: (a) config knowledge lives once, server-side, ready for the admin UI G1 anticipates; (b) future mobile/kiosk consumers of /admin/pos-category get the same allowlist for free; (c) additive `featured` field on the JSON response is non-breaking. Alternative (frontend computed filter) duplicates the allowlist into Vue and means PosComponent.vue is the only enforcement point.

title: OSS service does NOT explicitly exclude DELIVERY — a delivery order WITH token would surface on the customer wall today
evidence: Both list() (lines 45-52) and listForBranch() (lines 150-156) gate via `whereNotNull('token').orWhere(order_type, KIOSK=25).orWhere(order_type=TAKEAWAY=10 AND queue_number NOT NULL)`. A DELIVERY order (order_type=5) with a non-null `token` matches the first OR-branch and would appear on the wall. OrderType.php:7 `const DELIVERY = 5;`. No `where('order_type','!=',DELIVERY)` exists anywhere in this service.
recommendation: Per plan T-2.1.1, add `->where('order_type', '!=', \App\Enums\OrderType::DELIVERY)` to BOTH list() (after line 52, inside the same query chain) and listForBranch() (after line 156). Keep query bodies byte-identical per the service's own docstring line 144. Use the existing `OssPolishClusterTest::setUp` pattern (seedSpatieRoles + seedMinimalSettings) for the new feature test.

title: DBA: existing indexes adequate for the new `order_type != 5` clause — no schema change needed
evidence: Existing indexes on orders: PRIMARY(id), unique (branch_id,idempotency_key), unique (branch_id,fiscal_sequence_no), unique (branch_id,business_date,queue_number), idx_orders_branch_status (branch_id,status), idx_orders_user_id, idx_orders_datetime (order_datetime), idx_orders_status (status), orders_parent_order_id_index. The OSS query already narrows via idx_orders_branch_status (branch_id+status IN [7,8]) and idx_orders_datetime (today range). order_type filter applied to that already-small row-set is cheap; no new composite needed.
recommendation: No DDL. Document in implementer notes that `order_type != 5` is a post-filter on the already-tight (branch_id, status, today) result set. If a future profile shows the filter dominating, consider extending idx_orders_branch_status → (branch_id, status, order_type) — but defer until measured.
